newsitem.title: USA: Fiscal emergency declared for Ohio school district.
newsitem.headline: Fiscal emergency declared for Ohio school district.

text.p: Youngstown City School District became the first district in Ohio to be declared in a fiscal emergency under a new state law.

Ohio Auditor Jim Petro on Friday announced the fiscal emergency due to the district's financial crisis, which includes a $11.28 million fiscal 1997 operating deficit that represents 20 percent of general operating fund revenues in fiscal 1996.

Petro pointed out the district also met other criteria for a fiscal emergency, including $11.65 million in debt borrowed in fiscal 1996 and its need to borrow more money this fiscal year to repay the debt, as well as the fact the district did not pass a levy last year to tackle its debt and deficit problems.

"The failure of the area steel industry and other businesses has contributed to dwindling revenues for this district, while many student needs have increasesd," Petro said in a news release. "The district needs to quickly focus on a recovery plan."

The fiscal emergency law for school districts was passed by the Ohio Legislature earlier this year and took effect Sept. 19. Under the law, districts declared to be in a fiscal emergency will come under the oversight of a financial planning and supervision commission.
